title: A regular system of parameters is a regular sequence
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d$ and let $x_1,\dots,x_d\in\mathfrak m$ generate $\mathfrak m$ (a regular system of parameters; in a regular local ring these are exactly the minimal sets of generators of $\mathfrak m$). Then $x_1,\dots,x_d$ is a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and for each $0\le c\le d$ the ring $R/(x_1,\dots,x_c)$ is a regular local ring of dimension $d-c$. Since every permutation of $x_1,\dots,x_d$ again generates $\mathfrak m$, every permutation is a regular sequence.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM): 'Let R be a regular local ring and let x_1,...,x_d be a minimal set of generators for the maximal ideal m. Then x_1,...,x_d is a regular sequence, and each R/(x_1,...,x_c) is a regular local ring of dimension d-c'

proof.text: For a prefix of length c <= d, let I be its generated ideal. The parameter definition gives rs.length = d and I <= m. Thus R/I is nonzero, local and Noetherian. Its maximal ideal is the image of m, generated by the images of rs.drop c: the prefix maps to zero and the full list spans m.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NQ, dimension-squeezing proof; Definition Tag 00KU; Lemma Tag 00KW iterated; Nakayama Tag 00DV. Source verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NQ and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00KU, 2026-10-12.

proof.text: The maximal ideal of R/I has spanFinrank at most d-c, because the remaining list has that length. The local dimension bound gives dim(R/I) <= d-c. Krull height bounds for the c prefix equations give d <= dim(R/I)+c (Mathlib ringKrullDim_le_ringKrullDim_quotient_add_card, the local maximal-ideal specialization of lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound). Squeezing gives dim(R/I)=d-c and its embedding dimension is at most that dimension, so R/I is regular local. This works for c=0 and c=d too.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NQ, dimension-squeezing proof; Definition Tag 00KU; Lemma Tag 00KW iterated; Nakayama Tag 00DV. Source verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NQ and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00KU, 2026-10-12.

proof.text: For i < d, the regular local prefix quotient R/I_i is a domain by lem-sc-regular-local-domain. The next parameter rs[i] is not in I_i: otherwise I_(i+1)=I_i, while step 2 gives their quotient dimensions d-(i+1) and d-i, a contradiction. The nonzero image of rs[i] therefore has injective multiplication. Mathlib isSMulRegular_quotient_iff_mem_of_smul_mem transfers this to the module quotient in the definition of weak regularity. Since all parameters lie in m, IsLocalRing.isRegular_iff_isWeaklyRegular_of_subset_maximalIdeal (local Nakayama) gives regularity.

proof.text: A list permutation preserves membership and length, hence the regular-system-of-parameters predicate. Apply Mathlib IsLocalRing.isRegular_of_perm to the regular sequence from step 3. Pair this with step 2 to assemble the first theorem.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NQ, dimension-squeezing proof; Definition Tag 00KU; Lemma Tag 00KW iterated; Nakayama Tag 00DV. Source verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NQ and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00KU, 2026-10-12.

proof.text: For the minimal-generator characterization, lift the finite generating set s into m and map it to the cotangent space. Extract an independent subset b spanning the same cotangent space using exists_linearIndepOn_extension. CotangentSpace.span_image_eq_top_iff (Nakayama) says b still generates m, so minimality implies its underlying finset is s. IsLocalRing.spanFinrank_maximalIdeal_eq_ncard identifies its cardinality with the embedding dimension, which equals d by regularity. Conversely, a proper subset of a d-element generating set has fewer than d members and cannot generate m by the dimension bound.

lean.statement: theorem isRegular_and_quotients_of_generators (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsRegularLocalRing R] (d : ℕ) (hd : ringKrullDim R = (d : WithBot ℕ∞)) (rs : List R) (hrs : IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters rs) : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R rs ∧ (∀ c : ℕ, c ≤ d → IsRegularLocalRing (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (rs.take c)) ∧ ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Ideal.ofList (rs.take c)) = ((d - c : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧ (∀ ys : List R, rs.Perm ys → IsLocalRing.IsRegularSystemOfParameters ys ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R ys)
